failed_hosted_matrix.head: 954213c4aa3ef40dd3716e556d53fa39e5d23644
failed_hosted_matrix.diagnosis: All failures are the two lower-version capture fixture capability choices and/or nohup readiness predicate. Production runtime unchanged by test corrections.

capture_fixture.baseline: Reproduced both hosted CPython3.11 failures locally: the two active PythonCapture fixtures implicitly requested default monitoring, which correctly rejects3.10/3.11 unless legacy is explicit.
capture_fixture.implementation: Only tests/test_review_injob_trace.py changes: pass legacy=sys.version_info<(3,12) in the stalled-fsync test and generated near-recursion program. Newer versions retain sys.monitoring. No runtime fallback or default changed.
capture_fixture.assertions_preserved: No skips or weakened assertions:100calls remain nonblocking while flush fsync stalls; complete prefix, one metadata dictionary and exact calls remain checked. Recursion depth985 at limit1000 must succeed before and during capture with child exit0 on every interpreter.
capture_fixture.qualification: Whole-file functional regressions, run concurrently; timings are not controlled performance measurements. Runtime bytes are unchanged by this followup.

terminal_fixture.issue: Bash background PID publication did not establish that nohup had installed SIGHUP-ignore before terminal close.

runtime_review.ownership: signal_owned targets the live owned launcher/shell process group and the kernel-reported foreground group. It does not enumerate or terminate the whole terminal session. Maintenance closes the PTY and reaps already-exited children; it does not kill background nohup groups.
runtime_review.child_signal_setup: Terminal child launcher resets SIGHUP to default before exec, so inherited SIG_IGN in the workload establishes actual nohup behavior.

result.fixture: Real Bash PTY background child held at an explicit before-exec FIFO barrier; this exposes the PID-publication contract without a timing sleep.
result.conclusion: Bash $! readiness admits a live child before nohup has installed SIGHUP-ignore; this is a readiness-fixture defect, not a claim that an established nohup workload was killed.

old_predicate_reproduction.limits: Explicit FIFO barrier deterministically exposes pre-exec readiness; this is not a claim to have observed the original hosted process scheduling.

fixture_change.readiness: Actual nohup launches a Python workload. The workload asserts signal.getsignal(SIGHUP)==SIG_IGN, then publishes os.getpid(). No test code installs the ignored disposition itself.
preserved_assertions: owned child still exists after the original post-close poll interval
finally kills only the fixture-owned published PID; service context performs owned cleanup

result.readiness: Actual nohup workload verifies inherited SIGHUP=SIG_IGN before publishing its own PID.
result.assertions: close accepted; child exists after close; child is not zombie; finally SIGKILL only the fixture-owned PID; TerminalService context closes/reaps owned service.
result.limits: Software process/signal qualification on local Linux; duration is not a performance benchmark. No arbitrary readiness sleep.

Whole-file and repetition durations are test evidence, not performance benchmarks.
Hosted replacement matrix remains required; no macOS, GPU, Slurm or remote qualification is inferred.

acceptance: Keep the nonblocking callback, exact metadata, recursion985/limit1000, established-nohup survival, nonzombie and owned cleanup assertions. Use explicit supported capture mode and actual child readiness rather than skipping or relaxing them.
qualification_limit: Focused test corrections qualify their actual checks; all hosted Python suites and subsequent packaging checks must pass on the replacement delivered tree before merge.
